pattern.crimePattern: recipient of money sent to the wrong number kills the sender who tracked her down
pattern.notes: Mistaken mobile-money transfers and failed reversals are an everyday hazard in Kenya; fictional service, numbers masked, no real case.

ob.text: A porter reports that tomato wholesaler Everlyne Nasimiyu (36) was found dead behind the produce sheds at Kongowea market at 11:05.

facts.text: Tomato wholesaler Everlyne Nasimiyu was found dead behind the produce sheds at Kongowea market at 11:05.
Everlyne was struck with a 5 kg cast-iron weight from a scale.
Her phone is still in her apron.
Everlyne's phone, Monday 16:02: 'KSh 85,000 sent to MWANAIDI MWATSAHU 07xx xxx 309.'
Monday 16:10: 'Reversal request received.' 16:40: 'Reversal failed: recipient has insufficient balance.' Then 11 unanswered calls to that number.
Tuesday 10:05: an incoming call from 07xx xxx 309, two minutes.
A scrap in her apron: 'Benard lorry — 07xx xxx 390'. The lorry driver's number ends 390; the money went to one ending 309.
PesaPap, 07xx xxx 309: Monday 16:02 received KSh 85,000. 16:05, agent withdrawal of KSh 85,000.
Records, 07xx xxx 309, Tuesday: call to Everlyne at 10:05; Kongowea mast 10:20–10:55; 10:52 tuk-tuk fare from Kongowea.
Saidi: at about 10:40 he saw Everlyne arguing behind the sheds with a young woman carrying a pink phone pouch on a strap. Everlyne grabbed at the pouch.
Saidi was called to unload a lorry at 10:42 (the other porter confirms). Another porter found her at 11:05.
Mwanaidi's pink trade pouch: the strap clip is broken, and there is a tomato-juice stain on the flap.
Everlyne's receipt book: 12 crates sold at 10:35 to a hotel buyer, G. Mwangemi.
Benard's weighbridge ticket: Mariakani, in 10:30, out 10:44, outbound to Taveta; checkpoint stamp on the Taveta road at 11:20. Mariakani is about an hour from Kongowea.
Linet's bank queue ticket, town branch: issued 10:10, served 11:02.
Beatrice: Everlyne never went to the police. She meant to go after paying the lorry, and never had the time.
Beatrice: on Monday night Everlyne said she would "report that number to the police" if the money didn't come back.
Hotel delivery note: Godfrey left Kongowea in the hotel van at 10:37 and was unloading at the Nyali kitchen at 10:55.
Mwanaidi sells second-hand phones at Mwembe Tayari. She has no stall at Kongowea and doesn't trade tomatoes.
Mwanaidi: "That money came by mistake and I sent it straight back."
Mwanaidi: "I don't go to Kongowea. I sell phones at Mwembe Tayari. I've never met her."
Mwanaidi: "I needed it. My mother is in hospital."
Mwanaidi admits she went to Kongowea to tell Everlyne she would pay it back slowly. Everlyne shouted and grabbed her pouch; she says she pulled away and left.
Benard: "I was on the road back to Taveta."
Benard admits he told Everlyne, "No money, no more tomatoes." "She told me she'd sent it to the wrong number. I didn't believe her."
Linet: "I was at the bank."
Linet: she and Everlyne were splitting the business "politely". "Accountants, not shouting."

interrogations.intro: Mwanaidi keeps her hand flat on a phone she is pretending to repair. "Wrong number? It happens. I sent it back."

topics.reply: People mistype every day. It's not my fault what people type.

interrogations.intro: Benard talks from his cab over the noise of the engine. "Everlyne? Dead? I shouted at her yesterday."

topics.reply: No money, no more tomatoes, I told her. She swore she'd sent it to the wrong number. I thought she was lying. God forgive me.

interrogations.intro: Linet answers from a bank queue. "I am number forty-one and they are serving thirty-six. What is it?"

topics.reply: We were splitting up the business. Politely. Accountants, not shouting.
Benard threatened her yesterday. No money, no more tomatoes. Everyone heard.

interrogations.intro: Saidi wipes his face with his vest. "I saw them fighting. I didn't think it was serious. People fight here every hour."

topics.reply: Young. A cap. That pink pouch. Mama Everlyne grabbed it like she wanted to tear it off her.

interrogations.intro: Godfrey takes the call in a hotel kitchen, pans clattering. "Twelve crates at half past ten. She was fine. She was laughing."
Beatrice holds her sister's phone in both hands. "She told me about the money last night. She was so angry."

topics.reply: That name was on the message. Everlyne said it over and over last night. Mwanaidi Mwatsahu.

contradictions.reaction: I needed it. My mother is in hospital, they want forty thousand before they operate. Eighty-five thousand just arrived. Like God sent it. I took it out before I could think.
I went to tell her I'd pay it back. Slowly. She shouted. She grabbed my pouch. I pulled away and I left. That's all. That's all.

words.text: she wouldn't return money sent to her by mistake
a fight over a stolen phone
Everlyne had reported her to the police

prosecutor.pass: Out in three minutes, a call on Tuesday, the Kongowea mast, and a pouch with a broken clip. That will hold.
fail: Doesn't hold up. The lorry driver threatened her, but he was an hour up the Taveta road. Who was behind those sheds?
No. Read the number on the scrap of paper against the number the money went to.

prosecutor.pass: A reversal fails when the money's already out. Whoever withdrew it in three minutes knew exactly what they had.
fail: She did it, but that isn't why. Read the reversal message.
There's no police report, and her phone is in her apron. Try again.

proof.concludes: Everlyne meant to pay Benard (…390) and sent KSh 85,000 to …309 instead: Mwanaidi Mwatsahu. The reversal failed.
Mwanaidi withdrew all of it three minutes after it arrived. On Tuesday she called Everlyne and her phone was at Kongowea from 10:20 to 10:55. Pressed, she admits meeting her.
At 10:40 Everlyne grabbed at a young woman's pink pouch behind the sheds. Mwanaidi's pink pouch has a broken clip and a tomato stain. Mwanaidi killed her over money she wouldn't give back.

eliminations.why: Benard was at the Mariakani weighbridge at 10:30 and on the Taveta road by 11:20, about an hour away.
Linet was in a bank queue in town from 10:10 to 11:02.
Saidi was unloading a lorry from 10:42 until the body was found.
Godfrey left in the hotel van at 10:37 and was unloading in Nyali at 10:55.
Everlyne's phone is still in her apron, and nothing of Mwanaidi's was taken.
The tomato debt is Benard's grievance. Mwanaidi doesn't trade tomatoes.
Mwanaidi has no stall at Kongowea.
Everlyne never went to the police.

reconstruction.text: Monday, 16:02. Everlyne sends KSh 85,000 for the lorry. One digit is wrong: 309, not 390.
16:05. Mwanaidi sees the message and withdraws all of it at an agent. Everlyne's reversal fails at 16:40. Eleven calls go unanswered.
Tuesday, 10:05. Mwanaidi calls back at last. At 10:20 she is at Kongowea.
10:40, behind the sheds. Everlyne grabs her pouch so she can't walk away. A 5 kg weight from the nearest scale.
10:52. A tuk-tuk from Kongowea, paid by phone, with a broken pouch strap.
